product.title: A team of coding agents, on your desk, under your rules
product.lede: You describe a task. Rotaris classifies it and hands it to a coordinator, which delegates to specialists — an analyst, an architect, coding agents, a tester and more. The run works through a todo list one item at a time and checks what it changed before it decides what comes next.
product.closing: You see every agent while it works, every tool call passes a permission you set, and every run can be taken back.

orchestration.title: Orchestration
orchestration.body: A coordinator that delegates to 13 built-in specialist roles, in parallel where the work allows it.

control.title: Control
control.body: Steer an agent, queue a follow-up, edit the todo list, switch the model, pause or cancel — without restarting.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.body: Every tool call resolves to allow, ask or deny at one gate before it runs, and lands in an audit trail.

recovery.title: Recovery
recovery.body: A checkpoint after each iteration that changed your tree, and every session kept on your machine.

howItWorks.title: From one sentence to a result you can check

classify.title: Say what you want done
classify.body: Type the task into the composer and press Run. Rotaris classifies its intent first, so the coordinator starts from what kind of work it is.
classify.control: the task, and the permission mode

plan.title: A coordinator, not a soloist
plan.body: The orchestrator keeps a todo list and hands every work item to a specialist. While it coordinates it does not edit files or run commands itself.

delegate.title: The right specialist for each item
delegate.body: Codebase analyst, architect, planner, coding agent, tester, docs writer, refactorer, verifier and more — each role brings its own instructions and the tools it is granted.

run.title: Parallel where it can, asked where it must
run.body: Independent items run side by side. Every tool call meets the permission gate first; whatever the mode says to ask about waits for your answer.

verify.title: Checked before it moves on
verify.body: Each iteration that changed the tree is verified with deterministic checks and closed with a checkpoint. Failed work is re-queued with the evidence attached.
verify.control: skipping a check, if you must

review.title: Your call, last
review.body: The run ends with a stop reason and a status. Read the diff in the Git view, keep the result — or restore any checkpoint and try again.

views.title: Six views. One session in frame.
views.lede: The session you are working on never leaves the screen. Around it, everything Rotaris knows — agents, requirements, worktrees, artifacts, configuration — has one visible home, and every view and common action has a keyboard chord.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.body: The live transcript of messages, reasoning, grouped tool calls and diffs; the composer with slash commands and image attachments; and the inspector for the agent you follow.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: The delegation tree, what every agent is doing and what it has cost, context use per agent, provider standing, and the workspace's sessions.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.body: Your project's own requirements as cards with the health of the evidence behind them. An agent surveys the repository to propose their shape, and the board starts the runs that deliver them.

git.title: Git
git.body: Session worktrees, changed files and diffs, and the checkpoint taken after each iteration — any of which can be restored.

library.title: Library
library.body: The artifacts agents publish, your saved prompts, and improvement proposals from post-run analysis — reviewed, then applied by a checkpointed run.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Providers and model slots, the permission mode and its rules, tools, MCP servers, hooks, and three built-in themes — layered YAML underneath, edited here.

orchestration.title: A stable center. Specialists in motion.
orchestration.lede: The orchestrator plans and delegates; 13 built-in roles do the work. Each child agent is handed one slice, works with the tools its role grants, and returns a report the coordinator can act on.

parallelism.lead: Parallel where the work is independent.
parallelism.body: The coordinator delegates side by side and waits only when it needs a result.

coordinatorOnly.body: While it coordinates it does not modify files or run commands; every work item reaches a specialist.

bounded.body: Limits, timeouts and a hidden loop monitor make sure no run ends with work or child agents left hanging.

reports.body: Each child ends with a machine-readable report artifact that carries the answer it ended on.

cancellation.body: Stop a parent and every descendant stops with it — cleanly.

improvement.body: A post-run analysis proposes improvements to the Library; you review them, and a checkpointed run applies the ones you accept.

diagram.alt: Radial diagram: the orchestrator at the center — shown as a small net spanning delegation intensity per agent — delegating to seven specialist agents arranged in an even ring, each colored by state — done, running, or waiting

verification.title: Every change, checked and traced
verification.lede: Your requirements stay versioned documents in your own repository. Rotaris compiles them into symbols your code and tests reference, and checks that every approved requirement is implemented and covered — and that nothing drifted.

chain.requirementBody: Session handlers shall be non-blocking under load.
chain.taskBody: Convert session handlers to async · coding-agent-1

gate.title: Checked before the run moves on
gate.body: Every iteration that changed the tree is verified with deterministic checks before the run decides what to do next. Work that fails is re-queued with the evidence, or abandoned with a reason — never quietly marked done. A verifier role can grade the result against your original request.
gate.traceability: The Requirements board reads the same data: an agent surveys your repository and proposes how its requirements are shaped, respects the acceptance criteria and status fields already there, and starts the runs that deliver them. Nothing is written by merely looking at the board.

band.lead: Free and open source under GPL-3.0-only.
band.note: No account required — download, open a project folder, bring your own model.

control.title: Supervised autonomy, fully observable
control.lede: Every agent's state, tool, elapsed time, context window and model stay visible while the run is live — and every control either takes effect with stated timing or tells you why it can't.

human.body: Steer an agent mid-task, queue a follow-up, edit the todo list, switch the model, reasoning level or permission mode, force a context compression, pause, or cancel — cancellation cascades to every descendant.

failure.body: Failures surface as visible states. The run re-queues the item with the failing evidence attached, and notices say what failed and how to recover.

models.title: Your models, your keys
models.lede: Sign in once and Rotaris discovers what a provider offers, then fills its model slots — large, medium, small, summary and fallback — automatically. Change any slot, or switch a live run's model and reasoning level without restarting.
models.overrides: The reasoning choices follow what the selected model actually supports.
models.note: Rotaris Cloud, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, your Claude subscription through Claude Code, DeepSeek, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — including models running on your own machine. Quota and credit standing stay visible before you hit a limit.

security.title: Nothing runs unasked
security.lede: An agent left alone in a repository can run a command you did not want or write outside the project. Each of those has a mechanism here — and the mode you choose is the mode the run gets, never silently downgraded.

gate.title: One permission gate
gate.body: Every tool call resolves to allow, ask or deny before it runs. Three modes — restricted, ask, autonomous — plus starter rules that deny recursive deletes, privilege escalation, force pushes and package publishing.

files.title: Workspace path fence
files.body: File tools are fenced to the workspace; a path outside it fails instead of being read or written.

network.title: Network egress and confinement
network.body: A per-host egress policy for fetches, and optional operating-system confinement of terminal commands through bubblewrap on Linux.

hooks.title: Hooks stay inert until approved
hooks.body: Lifecycle hooks a repository declares do nothing until you have reviewed and approved them.

secrets.title: Audited, with secrets redacted
secrets.body: Every permission decision is written to a per-session audit trail, with known secrets redacted. Provider credentials stay in machine-local files only your user account can read.

cancel.title: Cancellation, always
cancel.body: Any run, any agent, any time — cancellation propagates through the whole delegation tree.

where.local: The application and every run execute on your machine. Your repository is never uploaded.
where.providers: Only the prompts and code context a task needs are sent to the model provider you choose — Rotaris Cloud among them, if you pick it. With a local model, nothing leaves the machine.
where.telemetry: No telemetry and no usage statistics. Sessions and the audit trail stay in a machine-local store, workspace configuration in <0>.rotaris/</0> inside your project, global configuration in <1>~/.config/rotaris/</1>.
where.update: The one connection Rotaris opens by itself is the update check against GitHub's latest release, which tells GitHub your IP address and client details. An update is downloaded only after the signed checksum manifest has been verified.

security.permissionsLink: Permissions, modes, and rules in the documentation

git.title: Every iteration, a way back
git.lede: A session can work in a Git worktree of its own, so parallel sessions never trample each other. After each iteration that changed the tree, Rotaris records a checkpoint — and any of them can be restored from the Git view.

openSource.title: Built in the open
openSource.lede: Released under GPL-3.0-only, CI-built from tagged commits and shipped with checksums and an SBOM. The source stays open, and distributed modifications must remain available under the same copyleft terms.
openSource.note: Every release is built by CI from a tagged commit and published to GitHub Releases with a CycloneDX SBOM per platform. Earlier versions stay available.

what.a: A desktop application that carries a coding task to a result in your project with a team of AI agents: a coordinator that plans and delegates, and specialists that do the work — all of it visible, permission-gated and recorded.

status.a: Rotaris is pre-release. The current builds are release candidates for Windows x64 and Linux x86_64 and update themselves from GitHub. Expect rough edges, and report them on GitHub.

code.q: Does my code leave my computer?
code.a: The application and its runs execute locally, and your repository is never uploaded. The prompts and code context a task needs go to the model provider you choose — with a local model, nothing leaves the machine. The only connection Rotaris makes on its own is the update check against GitHub.

providers.q: Which model providers can I use?
providers.a: Rotaris Cloud, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, DeepSeek, your Claude subscription through Claude Code, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local models. Rotaris discovers each provider's models and fills its model slots for you.

subscription.q: Can I use my existing Claude or Copilot subscription?
subscription.a: Yes. A Claude subscription is used through the Claude Code tool you installed and signed in to — Rotaris detects it and never handles your Claude credentials. GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex sign in through their own browser or device-code flows.

permissions.q: Can an agent run anything it likes?
permissions.a: No. Every tool call passes one permission gate — allow, ask or deny — before it runs, and every decision is recorded. You pick the mode: restricted, ask (the default) or autonomous. Even autonomous keeps the deny rules for recursive deletes, privilege escalation, force pushes and package publishing.

undo.q: What if a run makes a mess?
undo.a: Rotaris records a checkpoint after each iteration that changed your tree. Restore any of them from the Git view. Sessions can also run in a worktree of their own, away from your working copy.

cancel.q: Can I pause or cancel a run?
cancel.a: At any time. Cancellation propagates through the delegation tree, so stopping a parent cleanly stops all of its descendants. You can also steer an agent, edit the todo list or switch the model without restarting.

cli.a: No. Rotaris is a graphical desktop application only, built to run beside your editor and terminal. Every view and common action has a keyboard chord, and the composer takes slash commands.

security.q: How do I report a security issue?
security.a: Through the repository's security policy on GitHub — see the security section for the disclosure process and response expectations.
